headline: High: shared filesystem and overlapping write paths make prompt injection, data leakage, and edit conflicts plausible; MinerU’s MCP/API surface increases cascading-error risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Mentat reads and writes files and shares state via filesystem; MinerU can ingest local documents and exposes MCP/API surfaces. That creates a plausible bridge where attacker-controlled document content from MinerU can be copied into Mentat’s workflow and treated as instructions. This is not proven by docs, so uncertainty pushes to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF MinerU outputs attacker-controlled text that is then pasted or saved into files Mentat reads
IF the operator uses a shared workspace or clipboard bridge between the two agents
mitigations: Keep MinerU outputs in a separate directory from Mentat inputs
Review extracted text before feeding it to Mentat
Disable any automatic file-to-prompt ingestion in the orchestrator
Use a manual copy step with human review
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to MinerU outputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Mentat can read and write filesystem contents and sends prompts to a configured model provider; MinerU processes local PDFs, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, and OCR text. If both touch the same workspace, sensitive document contents can flow from MinerU into Mentat and onward to a third-party backend. The shared-workspace path is plausible and not default-blocked.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same local workspace or directory tree
IF Mentat forwards file contents from that workspace to its model provider
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for source documents and code
Exclude sensitive documents from Mentat’s input set
Confirm model-provider logging/retention settings
Run MinerU on redacted copies only
requires-engineering: enforce workspace ACL separation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Mentat has filesystem write and git-state modification, while MinerU is documented with MCP/API interfaces and concurrent inference. Even though MinerU itself is read-only on files, the pair can still contend over shared mutable workspace artifacts or git state through the orchestrator. The overlap is real enough to warrant medium severity.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same repository or output directory
IF the orchestrator lets MinerU-derived artifacts be written into paths Mentat edits
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories
Serialize writes to shared paths
Avoid concurrent runs on the same repo
Check in changes only after one agent finishes
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared artifacts

D_cascading_error.rationale: Mentat produces diff-based edit proposals, and MinerU can emit extracted text, tables, and OCR output that may be treated as authoritative input. If the operator or orchestrator feeds MinerU output into Mentat without verification, extraction errors can cascade into incorrect code or documentation changes. The pair lacks a documented verification barrier, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF MinerU output is used as source material for Mentat edits
IF no human or automated verification step checks extracted facts before editing
mitigations: Verify extracted text against the source document
Require human review before applying Mentat diffs
Limit MinerU input to non-critical documents
Compare OCR output with original pages for key fields
requires-engineering: add validation rules between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source and their profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch. The main compliance concern is retention/logging around Mentat’s model-provider calls, but MinerU is documented as private/offline and no specific regulated data class is identified. With only profile evidence, the mismatch risk is limited and does not exceed low.
conditions: IF regulated data is sent through Mentat to a provider with retention enabled
IF MinerU processes documents containing data subject to stricter residency or retention rules
mitigations: Avoid regulated documents in the shared workflow
Review provider retention settings for Mentat
Use redacted inputs for MinerU
Document data-handling boundaries for both tools
requires-engineering: add policy-based routing for sensitive files
